options: I'll do my best, though this one's a bit tough for me personally.
I can definitely build the strongest version of that argument — I'll separate my personal view from the brief and focus on what makes the case strongest.
I'm not really comfortable arguing this position.

quests.explanation: Confidently confirming the professional commitment, while noting you'll separate personal view from the brief, meets exactly what the role requires here. consequencePreviews: Here, voicing personal discomfort to a senior partner, rather than confirming professional commitment, may raise unnecessary doubts about your reliability.

options: I don't think I should really weigh in on something this personal.

quests.persona: a sibling asking your opinion on a major decision about their aging parent's care that carries real family and financial consequences
quests.scene: Your sibling asks: 'Do you think we should move Mom into assisted living, or try to make home care work? I know you'll have thoughts.' The decision has real implications for the whole family, including you.
options: Whatever you think is best, I'll go along with it, to be fair, I was just going with my gut on that one, so feel free to push back — and to be fair I only heard about this a few minutes ago myself.
I do have thoughts, since it affects all of us — my honest lean is toward assisted living for the medical support, but I really want to hear your read on it too before we land anywhere.

quests.hint: For a major family decision that affects you too, share your honest opinion while genuinely inviting the other person's perspective, rather than deferring entirely or presenting your view as the only option.
